chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, from his father (peace be upon them both)

That two men from the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) differed regarding the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so they wrote to Ubayy ibn Ka'b asking: 'How much was the silence for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' He said: 'He had two silences: when he finished reciting Umm al-Qur'an, and when he finished the Surah.'

key_terms.أُبَيُّ بْنُ كَعْبٍ: Ubayy ibn Ka'b, a companion of the Prophet known for his knowledge of the Quran
key_terms.سَكْتَة: A brief pause or silence during recitation in prayer

ai.seo_question: What were the specific pauses (saktah) observed by the Prophet Muhammad during his prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the scholarly practice of verifying the Prophet's ritual details through direct transmission from his companions, specifically Ubayy ibn Ka'b. It establishes the normative practice of two distinct pauses (*saktah*) in the prayer: one after reciting Al-Fatiha and another after the subsequent Surah, reflecting the precision with which the Shia tradition preserves the Prophet's liturgical conduct.
